newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air travellers suffer Easter misery in France.
newsitem.headline: Air travellers suffer Easter misery in France.

text.p: A strike by ground staff forced state-owned airline Air France Europe to cancel all flights from Paris' Orly airport on Saturday, causing more misery for travellers on the busy Easter weekend.
Tempers ran high at the airport, south of the capital, as passengers found their holiday weekend in tatters.
The surprise stoppage at Air France Europe, which runs domestic and some European flights, had caused caused major cancellations and long delays at Orly on Friday.

A company spokeswoman said some 250 flights from Orly were cancelled but 89 flights from Charles de Gaulle airport, north of the capital, and flights between provincial cities were expected to go ahead.
Ground workers were protesting against the unifying of their pay and employment terms with those of parent company Air France in a merger between the two airlines.
Air France Europe pilots and flight crew have called a two-day strike over pay and conditions for next Monday and Tuesday but the company said all flights would take place.

Pilots and ground staff at British Airways Plc's French subsidiary TAT European Airlines have staged a 24-hour strike against restructuring plans. on Friday, forcing the cancellation of about three-quarters of the airline's 180 scheduled flights.
